headline: US-Iran conflict drives oil to $85 and gold to record highs, while Microsoft and Google surged last night on AI strength — ASX finished slightly softer today.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped last night after reports of Azure cloud revenue growing 43% — a huge number that shows its AI business is firing on all cylinders. There's also talk of a 10-12% dividend increase. Analysts are pointing to $560 as the next target. A strong night for your biggest US holding.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet held firm last night, supported by strong AI-driven earnings and a dividend that's helping underpin its ~$4 trillion valuation. Revenue and earnings per share remain solid, and the stock is benefiting from broad optimism about Big Tech's AI monetisation.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up last night alongside the broader NASDAQ tech rally. No specific company news — it rode the coattails of general market optimism around tech.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF ticked up today on the ASX, following positive sentiment around AI names globally. Still sitting at a loss overall (-12.96%), but today's session was a small step in the right direction.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS nudged up slightly today — a modest bounce but nothing dramatic. Analysts are asking whether Pilbara can stage a sustainable recovery as lithium prices remain under pressure. It's still down nearly 20% on your total investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped slightly today as the ASX 200 finished a touch lower. Nothing to worry about — this is a broad diversified fund and a small daily move is completely normal noise.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had the worst day in the portfolio today, slipping just under 1%. Emerging markets are feeling the pressure of a slightly weaker AUD and broader risk-off sentiment tied to the US-Iran conflict and rising oil prices.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was essentially flat today on the ASX — barely moved. It tracks the broad US market, and last night's modest S&P dip is reflected here. Nothing significant to note.

watch_today.title: Microsoft surging on Azure AI growth — sit tight
watch_today.detail: MSFT jumped 1.68% last night after Azure cloud revenue hit 43% growth and a dividend hike of 10-12% was flagged. For a long-term holder, this is exactly the kind of result you want to see. No reason to do anything but hold — the AI story is playing out as hoped.

watch_today.title: Oil spiking on US-Iran war — watch flow-on effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil surged 2.28% to US$85 a barrel last night as the US-Iran conflict escalates with direct military strikes on Iranian missile launchers. Higher oil raises costs across the economy — inflation, transport, energy. Worth watching whether this pushes central banks (including the RBA) to keep rates higher for longer.

watch_today.title: VGE down today — emerging markets under pressure
watch_today.detail: Your Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF slipped 0.95% today, and it's your only holding still in the red on a total return basis (down $2.24). Geopolitical tension and a slightly weaker AUD are headwinds for this fund. Long-term thesis for emerging markets remains intact — hold for now, but keep an eye on the Iran situation.

watch_today.title: PLS still underwater — but ticking in the right direction
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals edged up 0.75% today but remains down nearly 20% on your total investment. Analysts are querying whether a sustainable lithium recovery is coming. Nothing has changed structurally — if you believe in the long-term lithium demand story (EVs, batteries), sit tight. Don't sell into weakness.

watch_today.title: GXAI — AI ETF creeping back, but still in the red
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF rose 0.8% today and is slowly recovering, but still down 12.96% overall. The AI sector fundamentals remain strong (see Microsoft and Google results). For a long-term holder, this is a hold — the thesis hasn't broken, the sector is just volatile.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike risk rising — watch this week
watch_today.detail: New analysis out today suggests Australians aren't responding to the RBA's signals about inflation, raising the risk of rate hikes. Higher rates are a headwind for growth stocks and property. Nothing to act on immediately, but worth keeping an eye on any RBA commentary this week.

world.summary: The US-Iran war is the dominant global story, with direct US military strikes on Iranian soil, rising oil prices, and internal US political tensions all colliding at once.

stories.title: US strikes Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island
stories.why_it_matters: US forces struck two Iranian missile launchers on Iran's Larak Island in the Persian Gulf, a significant escalation in the ongoing US-Iran war. This is a direct strike on Iranian territory, not just a proxy target. Oil prices jumped 2.28% to $85 a barrel in response — higher energy costs flow through to petrol prices and inflation for everyday Australians. The conflict is now directly threatening Gulf energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Military leaders warn Hegseth against expanding the Iran war
stories.why_it_matters: Senior US military commanders have reportedly pushed back against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's appetite to extend Iran war operations further. This internal friction is significant — it suggests even the US military is worried about where this conflict is heading. If political leaders override military advice and escalate, the consequences for regional stability and global energy markets could be severe.

stories.title: Iran war strikes on Gulf energy infrastructure — oil impacts mapped
stories.why_it_matters: Al Jazeera has mapped how strikes linked to the US-Iran war are hitting Gulf energy infrastructure — oil terminals, tanker routes, and production facilities are all under threat. The Persian Gulf carries about 20% of the world's oil supply. Any sustained disruption could push oil well above $85, hitting Australian petrol prices and adding to inflation pressure that the RBA is already struggling to tame.

stories.title: Long-term investors piling into shipping as Middle East conflict pays off
stories.why_it_matters: With Middle East shipping routes disrupted by the Iran conflict, long-term institutional investors are betting big on shipping companies — because when ships have to take longer routes around conflict zones, freight rates spike and shipping firms profit. This is a reminder that geopolitical crises create winners as well as losers. Ordinary investors can access this theme through diversified ETFs, though it comes with political risk.

stories.title: Trump targets individuals including James Comey — growing list of administration targets
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has compiled and is acting on a list of political targets — including former FBI Director James Comey. This is part of a broader pattern of using the machinery of government against perceived political opponents. The list signals an increasingly assertive White House heading into the 2026 US midterm elections, with implications for the rule of law and institutional independence that investors globally are watching closely.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was modestly negative — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both dipped, though Big Tech names like Microsoft and Google bucked the trend. Oil surged on Iran tensions, gold hit fresh highs, and the Aussie dollar slipped slightly. The ASX 200 closed today down 0.18% — a quiet, slightly soft day.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft close today — down 16 points. Nothing alarming, just a bit of caution from investors watching oil and the Iran situation.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session was mildly negative, slipping 0.25%. Most sectors were cautious, though tech was a bright spot.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The tech-heavy NASDAQ dipped 0.52% last night overall, though Microsoft and Google individually rallied strongly — most of the drag came from smaller tech names.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big mover last night — up 2.28% as US military strikes on Iran's Larak Island rattled energy markets. Watch this one closely.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold edged up again to near $4,500 USD/oz — investors parking money in safe havens amid geopolitical tension.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped slightly — down 0.46% to 71.6 US cents. A weaker AUD makes your US holdings worth more in AUD terms, which is a small positive for MSFT, GOOG, and TTWO.

politics.summary: The RBA is back in focus, with analysts warning Australians aren't responding to rate signals — raising the prospect of more hikes to come.

stories.title: Rate hikes back on the table as Australians ignore RBA warnings
stories.why_it_matters: New analysis published today suggests that Australians are not moderating their spending in response to the Reserve Bank of Australia's messaging about inflation — which is exactly what the RBA needs to happen before it can cut rates. If consumers keep spending, the RBA may be forced to lift interest rates further rather than cut them. This matters for anyone with a mortgage, a business loan, or growth-oriented investments — higher rates for longer squeeze household budgets and can drag on share prices.

ai.summary: The big AI theme today is regulation — governments, companies, and statisticians are all scrambling to figure out how to put guardrails on AI before it causes serious harm. Meanwhile, AI is already reshaping industries from law to government enforcement.

stories.title: 100 companies including OpenAI and Anthropic warn of escalating AI cyberattacks
stories.why_it_matters: More than 100 major AI and tech companies — including OpenAI and Anthropic — have jointly warned that AI-powered cyberattacks are escalating rapidly. Hackers are now using AI tools to automate and personalise attacks at a scale previously impossible. This is a double-edged story: it's a threat for businesses and governments, but it's also a massive tailwind for cybersecurity companies. If you're invested in the AI space (like through GXAI), the cybersecurity sub-sector is one to watch.

stories.title: 'It feels like early Covid': The messy scramble to regulate AI
stories.why_it_matters: CNN is drawing parallels between the current rush to regulate AI and the chaotic early days of Covid — everyone knows something must be done, but nobody agrees on what or how fast. Governments are passing patchwork laws at different speeds, creating a confusing landscape for companies trying to comply. The concern is that moving too slow risks harm, but moving too fast risks stifling innovation. For investors in AI stocks, regulatory uncertainty is a real risk factor to keep in mind.

stories.title: China's Jiangsu province uses AI to make enforcement and penalty decisions
stories.why_it_matters: China's Jiangsu province has started using AI systems to assist in regulatory investigations and to help determine financial penalties. This is a glimpse of how AI is being embedded into government decision-making — not just helping humans decide, but actively shaping outcomes. It raises big questions about transparency and fairness when an algorithm is partly responsible for fining or investigating a business. Expect more countries to follow suit, for better or worse.

stories.title: AI is transforming law — lawyers must now become 'solution providers'
stories.why_it_matters: A new report argues that AI is fundamentally changing what lawyers do — automating document review, contract analysis, and legal research that used to take junior lawyers weeks. The upshot is that legal firms will need fewer hours but more strategic, creative thinking. It's a shift happening across many professions: AI handles the grunt work, and humans need to add higher-level value. For everyday people, this could eventually mean cheaper legal services.

sport.summary: NRL Round 27 is locked and loaded — major news includes a Knights player copping a season-ending ban, the Rabbitohs securing their finals spot with a touching tribute win, and the Sharks seeing their top-four hopes collapse. AFL also features, with coaching succession talk at Collingwood and a Port Adelaide veteran extending.

stories.title: Knights star banned for the rest of the season after horror tackle
stories.why_it_matters: A Knights player has been handed a season-ending suspension after a horror tackle in Round 26. The Knights are already on a bye in Round 27, so the timing softens the immediate blow — but losing a key player to a ban this late in the season is a serious hit to their finals campaign. The incident is drawing plenty of attention for the severity of the tackle itself.

stories.title: Rabbitohs lock in finals spot with touching Arrow tribute and Latrell's return
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney locked in their finals berth with a win that came with an emotional backdrop — a tribute to the late Paul Arrow — and the timely return of star centre Latrell Mitchell. Latrell's fitness is huge for the Rabbitohs heading into September. The win confirms they'll be in the post-season, and with Latrell back, they're a genuine threat.

stories.title: Sharks' top-four hopes 'dead in the water' after Eels ambush
stories.why_it_matters: The Cronulla Sharks were ambushed by the Parramatta Eels in Round 26, and Fox Sports is reporting their top-four finals hopes are now effectively over. A top-four finish would have given them two cracks at the semis — losing that advantage makes their path to the grand final significantly harder. The Eels, meanwhile, are flying at the right time of year.

stories.title: Scott Pendlebury tipped as potential next Collingwood senior coach
stories.why_it_matters: AFL.com.au is floating Scott Pendlebury as a potential future Collingwood senior coach. The Magpies legend is in his final seasons as a player and has long been seen as a future leader of the club. No announcement has been made, but the speculation reflects growing succession planning conversations at one of the AFL's biggest clubs.

stories.title: Eels farewell 10 players as major roster overhaul begins
stories.why_it_matters: The Parramatta Eels are releasing 10 players at season's end as a major squad overhaul gets underway — notable given they're also in the middle of a finals push. CODE Sports has the full breakdown of who's leaving. It's a significant reshaping of the roster that will define what the Eels look like in 2027.
